title: Principal AI Developer Experience Architect
description:
Our Purpose

At SentinelOne , we are driven by a clear purpose: to give the advantage to those who secure our future. As AI reshapes how organizations build, operate, and innovate, the responsibility to protect them becomes more critical than ever. When you join SentinelOne , your work helps protect global enterprises, critical infrastructure, and the technologies shaping tomorrow. If you are motivated by meaningful challenges and want your impact to be real, measurable, and global, you will find purpose here.

About Us

SentinelOne is a company at the intersection of AI and security, pioneering a new operating model for cybersecurity. Our AI-native platform unifies protection across endpoint, cloud, identity, data, and AI systems to deliver autonomous detection and response with clarity and speed. By combining real-time analytics, intelligent automation, and a unified data foundation, we reduce noise, simplify complexity, and empower security teams to focus on what truly matters.

Our teams are builders, problem-solvers, and innovators committed to shaping the future of security. If you are excited to solve hard problems alongside talented, mission-driven people, we invite you to help us build a safer future for humanity.

What Are We Looking For?

We’re looking for people who are relentlessly curious and committed to continuous learning. AI is reshaping every function across our business, and we enable every team member, regardless of role or level, to build fluency in AI tools and concepts. Those who thrive here actively seek out new solutions, experiment thoughtfully, and apply what they learn to drive better, faster, smarter outcomes.

As a Principal AI Developer Experience Architect, you will serve as the technical authority for the AI engineering layer at SentinelOne , designing how enterprise-grade AI coding assistants and LLM platforms integrate into our engineering workflows. You will own the strategy and architecture that ensures AI-generated code is trustworthy, performant, and reliable by default for an 800+ developer organization. Your work will ensure our AI tooling investment is secure, governed, and measurably impactful across context management, prompt design, and AI-driven code review.
What Will You Do?
Primary responsibilities include:
Architect the AI Engineering Layer

• Define the end‑to‑end architecture for AI-augmented development at SentinelOne , centered on enterprise-grade AI coding assistants and LLM platforms integrated with our IDEs, CI/CD pipelines, and internal platforms.

• Design how large-context LLMs consume our codebase and documentation context so that AI assistance scales safely across hundreds of repos.

• Establish reusable patterns for agentic workflows with clear rollback and validation strategies.

Own AI Guardrails, Skills, and Standards

• Define and maintain SentinelOne AI Coding Standards and a global skills & requirements framework that all AI coding tools (our chosen AI coding assistants, PR bots, agents) must enforce, including language, framework, security, performance, and reliability patterns.

• Translate these standards into prompt templates, tool configurations, and policy‑as‑code so they are enforced automatically rather than via documentation alone.

• Partner with InfoSec, Data Governance, and Legal to ensure all AI tooling adheres to SentinelOne ’s AI Policies, data residency, and FedRAMP compliance requirements.

Implement AI-Driven Code Review and Safety as Code

• Lead the integration of AI-powered code review tools that use AST analysis and static/dynamic checks to enforce style, security, performance, and reliability standards before human review.

• Integrate AI review signals with our SRE observability stack (logs, metrics, traces) to correlate code changes with incidents and anomalies, closing the loop from PR to production behavior.

title: Engineering Manager, Postgres
description:
At Render, we’re building the modern cloud platform for developers creating AI-native, full-stack, multi-service applications. Our mission is to eliminate the tradeoff between the power of hyperscalers and the simplicity of developer-friendly platforms-so teams can ship fast, scale reliably, and focus on their product, not infrastructure.

Unlike complex hyperscalers or ephemeral edge/serverless solutions, Render offers a developer-first experience with persistent compute, dynamic autoscaling, built-in orchestration, and observability, allowing teams to launch, scale, and manage real-world applications without writing infrastructure code or managing servers. Whether you're building LLM-powered applications, scalable SaaS products, or async processing pipelines, Render empowers teams to move fast and scale confidently from MVP to millions of users.

Our platform is trusted by over 7 million developers worldwide and continues to grow rapidly. In February 2026, we raised an additional $100M in Series C financing, bringing our total funding to $260M, to accelerate our vision of making cloud infrastructure both powerful and intuitive-designed for the speed of modern AI development.

We’re a diverse and talented team that values craft, velocity, and user experience. If you’re excited to help shape the future of the intelligent cloud and empower developers everywhere, we’d love to hear from you.

APPLYING TO RENDER

We're seeking candidates who possess high integrity, humility, and an insatiable drive to learn. Through reasoned discussions and continuous feedback, we strive to improve both individually and collectively. We foster an environment of mutual trust and respect, empowering effective debate to achieve the best outcomes for our customers and team.

We especially encourage members of underrepresented groups in the tech community to apply and understand that not all successful candidates will meet each requirement listed.

Our interview process is unique to each role, and we value the candidate experience just as much as our customer experience. We hope your conversations with us reflect a thoughtful process that is illuminative, enjoyable, and respectful of your time.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As an Engineering Manager for Postgres, you will lead a group of talented engineers building and maintaining the Render Postgres product. This role blends strong technical leadership with product thinking: you’ll partner closely with product managers and designers to translate user needs into a high-quality, scalable system, that hundreds of thousands of developers rely on every day. You’ll be responsible for guiding technical direction, developing engineers, and ensuring the team ships meaningful improvements quickly while maintaining the high standards that define Render’s platform. The ideal candidate brings a strong engineering background, a deep sense of ownership, experience building stateful services, and a passion for building products that developers love.

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Lead and grow a team of postgres engineers, supporting their development through mentorship, feedback, and clear technical guidance.

- Drive execution on key product initiatives from ideation through launch, balancing speed with high standards of reliability and quality.

- Partner closely with Product, Design, and Infra teams to translate customer needs into thoughtful technical solutions and product roadmaps.

- Engage deeply in technical discussions, guiding system design decisions and helping the team navigate architectural tradeoffs.

- Foster a culture of ownership, accountability, and continuous improvement across engineering practices and team processes.

- Help the team break down complex problems into incremental milestones that deliver value quickly while supporting long-term platform evolution.

- Ensure teams maintain a strong understanding of the developer experience and customer impact of the features they build.

title: Consultant - Senior Consultant – Energy Policy and Regulation (Sydney or Melbourne)
description:
About Baringa 

Baringa is a global consulting firm that partners with leaders to drive change and create value. With deep industry expertise, and enabled by advanced technology, the firm helps clients to deliver with greater confidence and certainty. With over 2,000 people across the UK, Europe, North America, Asia and Australia, the firm combines global insight with local understanding.

The firm works across energy and resources, financial services, government and public sector, consumer products and retail, pharmaceuticals and life sciences, manufacturing, and technology, media and telecoms, with capabilities spanning strategy, transformation and operational excellence - all powered by advanced technology, data, AI and digital innovation.

Clients value Baringa’s collaborative approach and the way its teams integrate seamlessly - all working with a shared understanding of what matters most. The firm is known for its kind, curious experts who listen closely and care deeply about client success as they help clients transform energy markets, modernise financial platforms, expand telecoms and digital networks through advanced data analytics, enable digital services in government, and unlock growth in consumer sectors.

Certified as a  Great Place to Work around the world, Baringa has been recognised by the Financial Times in 22 categories of its UK Leading Management Consultants rankings, and by Forbes for four consecutive years as one of the World’s Best Management Consulting Firms.

Our Energy Policy and Regulation practice is looking for an experienced Consultant or Senior Consultant to join the team.  

Our Energy Policy and Regulation team in Australia works with organisations at the centre of the energy transition, including governments, regulators, market bodies, investors, developers, networks and retailers. We combine deep knowledge of electricity markets and networks with practical policy, regulatory and commercial insight, helping clients understand complex market changes and make confident decisions. Our work spans market reform, network regulation, consumer energy resources, wholesale market design, renewable energy zones, transmission planning and the role of policy in enabling a reliable, affordable and lower-carbon energy system. We mostly support clients in Australia’s east-coast National Electricity Market (NEM), along with some support to clients in Western Australia’s and New Zealand’s energy markets.

What you will be doing

Examples of the types of projects you can expect to work on:

• Advising policymakers on policy design for complex energy transition topics such as the integration of large-scale renewables and storage into market, the future role of networks, or the integration of data centres into the grid

• Working alongside the team of a government transmission planning body on the development and implementation of policy and regulations for renewable energy zones, access rights and transmission planning

• Supporting an energy network to develop their regulatory proposal to the Australian Energy Regulator (AER), including leading work on regulatory strategy, business case development, demand forecasting, cost-benefit analysis and stakeholder engagement

• Advising on the integration of consumer energy resources (CER) into the grid such as developing a distribution system operator (DSO) strategy for a distribution network, network tariff design, non-network solutions, or the role of the wholesale market, networks, retailers and aggregators to effectively optimise CER

• Advising clients on potential future options for wholesale market design to facilitate investment, drive the energy transition while maintaining reliability and affordability.

• Providing policy and regulatory insights into commercial advisory work across a range of project types such as market entry strategy for a new storage developer, due diligence on the sale of a transmission network, or commercial growth strat

title: Director of Finance
description:
This isn’t your regular job. Almedia is a place where those who want to push harder can accelerate their careers faster than anywhere else. We’re aiming to become Germany’s second bootstrapped unicorn. Almedia is already Europe’s #3 fastest-growing company in 2025 (FT1000).

We are building the future of marketing by rewarding our community of over 70 million users for engaging with our advertisers’ products. We are offering a new way to acquire users for the biggest companies in the world.

At Almedia, you’ll:

- Own way more, way earlier - you’ll be trusted with responsibility fast.

- Push harder, get further - this isn’t a 9-5. We highly reward intensity.

- Join a rare environment - you will work with ambitious high-speed, high-ownership people.

- Fully present - we’re 5 days a week in the office to build the energising momentum we need.

We’re looking for a Director of Finance to accelerate Almedia’s growth by leading strategic finance initiatives, FP&A, capital markets activities, and M&A execution. This is a highly hands-on role for a finance leader who can seamlessly move between high-level strategic planning, complex financial modeling, investor-ready communications, and hands-on deal execution.

This role sits at the intersection of corporate finance strategy, operational FP&A, and transaction execution. You will partner directly with leadership to evaluate build-vs-buy opportunities, build scalable financial frameworks, optimize capital structure, and drive clear, decision-grade analysis across the company.

You won’t just report the numbers - you will be a key partner in shaping Almedia’s financial roadmap, capital strategy, and long-term business growth.

Salary: 120-150k • Total Comp: 200k • Includes Equity

WHAT YOU’LL DO 🎯

- Drive Corporate Finance & Strategic Initiatives: Lead company-wide strategic finance projects, connecting financial analysis to business strategy, strategic trade-offs, and operational priorities.

- Lead FP&A and Decision-Grade Analysis: Build, refine, and maintain high-quality financial models, budget frameworks, scenario plans, and benchmarking metrics to guide internal growth decisions.

- Support Capital Markets & External Financing: Lead workstreams for equity and debt financing, preparing materials, financial narratives, and valuation analyses for discussions with external investors and partners.

- Execute M&A and Deal Strategy: Own M&A process execution from opportunity evaluation and diligence to financial impact analysis, valuation frameworks, and internal recommendations.

- Establish Repeatable Finance Processes: Build structured, scalable frameworks for transaction diligence, financial forecasting, and strategic evaluation to empower leadership to act quickly with confidence.

- Operate as a Hands-On Owner: Work directly in the details to build models and presentation decks yourself while independently driving complex strategic workstreams forward.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING 💡

- Comprehensive Strategic Finance Skill Set: Strong foundation across corporate finance, FP&A, capital markets, valuation, and M&A within a fast-moving, high-growth environment.

- Background in PE, Investment Banking, or High-Growth Finance: Experience in private equity, investment banking, corporate development, or strategic finance in a fast-paced operating company.

- Advanced Financial Modeling Rigor: Proven track record of independently building robust, dynamic financial models, forecasts, and scenario analyses from scratch.

- Commercial & Strategic Acumen: Ability to evaluate operational realities through a financial lens and distill findings into actionable strategic guidance.

- Executive-Level Communication: Skill in translating complex financial concepts, forecasts, and transaction structures into concise recommendations for leadership, board members, and investors.

- High Ownership Mindset: Self-driven, pragmatic, and eager to dive deep into details to push initiatives over the finish line.

title: Principal Product Manager, Discovery & Growth
description:
Find the right problem. Test the right theory. Build the right thing.

Spinwheel is on a mission to reinvent how consumers manage debt, make lending work for them, and move faster than anyone thinks possible. Our platform helps people save time, money, and stress by delivering the tools and intelligence needed to improve financial outcomes. We're hiring a Principal Product Manager, Discovery & Growth , to independently define and drive the discovery motion for Spinwheel 's future product roadmap. This is a Principal level individual contributor role for someone who has already run this kind of function, not someone learning to. You'll set the strategy for how we find, validate, and prove out net-new product and revenue opportunities before they compete for core roadmap investment, and you'll operate with minimal oversight in doing it. This role exists so that new bets get tested with rigor without derailing the core product organization, and so that nothing moves to full build without a proven connection to revenue. You'll report directly to the Head of Product and be trusted to run the full discovery-to-launch pipeline as its owner, not its executor.
What You'll Do

• Set the strategy and process for how Spinwheel finds unmet needs and whitespace in debt, lending, and consumer finance, spending real time with customers, prospects, internal teams, and market data to do it

• Independently shape raw opportunities into testable hypotheses and design the lean experiments (prototypes, concierge MVPs, pilots) that validate or kill them fast, without needing a playbook handed to you

• Build and present the business case for validated opportunities, including the revenue hypothesis and evidence, and drive joint go/no-go decisions with Product and Sales leadership

• Own full 0-to-1 execution end to end for anything that clears the gate, from launch through growth, making the calls on scope, sequencing, and trade-offs yourself

• Instrument products from day one and define what good measurement looks like for a bet at this stage of maturity

• Track post-launch performance against your original revenue hypothesis and turn every bet, proven or not, into an institutional lesson the broader product org can use

• Own and evolve a standing log of active opportunity hypotheses and their stage, visible to Product and Revenue leadership, as a management tool you use to run the function

• Act as the senior voice on industry trends, regulatory shifts, and adjacent market dynamics that could open new doors, and shape how Spinwheel thinks about them

What Success Looks Like

• You surface 2-3 high-conviction opportunities per quarter that the team didn't have on their radar, and your judgment on what's worth testing is trusted without much second-guessing

• You kill bad ideas fast and early, and your track record on when to kill versus back an idea becomes a reference point for the broader org

• You launch multiple net-new revenue-driving products or capabilities from 0-to-1 in your first year, run largely on your own judgment

• You become the senior connective tissue between customer reality and product strategy, shaping how leadership thinks about where to place bets

• Revenue and retention metrics improve because the problems you chose to solve mattered, and other teams start pointing to your process as the model for derisking new ideas

You're a Fit If You

• Have 8+ years in product management with a track record of owning outcomes at a senior or director level, including at least 3 years in fintech (debt, payments, credit, or lending a strong plus) building B2B products for enterprise customers .

• Have led 0-to-1 builds multiple times, ideally including at least one where you built and owned the discovery process itself, not just the execution

• Have deep, demonstrated rigor in testing unproven ideas and know when to kill an idea as confidently as when to back one, with real bets to point to on both sides

﻿The Company
Sunbit builds financial technology for real life. Our AI-native platform helps more people get to “yes” at the moments that matter with personalized offers, transparent terms, and no added consumer fees. In stores, practices and service centers across the country, Sunbit provides a fast, fair pay-over-time option. For everything else, the Sunbit Credit Card delivers a modern, no-fee credit experience managed in a powerful mobile app.
We are guided by people-centered values: Serve Others Before Self, Include Always, Connect Genuinely, Innovate for Good. These values shape how we build, how we support customers and merchants, and how we work with each other.
What makes Sunbit different is an AI-native infrastructure that runs through the full customer and merchant journey. Our interconnected AI systems power instant decisioning, streamline fraud checks with human-in-the-loop safeguards, and enable highly personalized offers at scale. The result is a quick, fair, and simple experience for consumers and merchants.
We pair this technology with inclusion and transparency. Sunbit delivers industry-leading approval rates - 90%+ in auto service and 85%+ in dental - while maintaining zero consumer fee-based revenue. It is a better way to serve people and merchants, proven at scale.
Today, Sunbit is available across a nationwide, in-person merchant network of 30,000+ locations spanning auto service centers, dental and optical practices, veterinary clinics, and other specialty services. We help teams say “yes” more often and help customers move forward with confidence.
The Role:
We are looking for a hands-on Director of Analytics to lead Merchant Ecosystem analytics. You will manage a team of senior analysts and work directly with Merchant and company leaders.
The role has two halves. First, you will own analytics self-serve: moving us from a model where business teams ask analysts for answers, to a governed, agent-enabled environment where they answer their own questions with data they trust. Second, you will own merchant and BNPL analytics, including the loan application funnel and loan performance.

Our subscription-based, direct-to-consumer model relies on technology at every step, from customer-facing apps and personalization logic to pricing, forecasting, supply chain optimization, and initiatives that help reduce food waste. Behavioral Data & Experimentation Platform is a cross-functional team with end-to-end ownership of digital tracking across all markets globally at HelloFresh - from infrastructure all the way to curated data products and the hypotheses validation mechanisms (eg. AB testing, quasi-experiments). The squad brings together software engineers, data engineers, and data scientists to build the tracking, event, and statistical infrastructure that every tech team relies on to drive product decisions. Our work enables customer experience improvements and business growth.

As our Senior Data Engineer, you'll play a crucial part in extending and operating the platform behind our behavioral data - from event & experiment pipelines to Databricks Unity Catalog and semantic layer integrations, to the systems and standards that let other teams validate hypotheses on top of our platform. This isn't a pure data pipeline-building role: you'll reason about system design, schema governance and develop a technology platform as much as data engineering. • Become an integral part of a high-impact data platform team, covering behavioral and experimentation data products.

• Design, build, and operate the platform components behind our behavioral data and experimentation infrastructure (Snowplow, Statsig, Databricks, Unity Catalog).

• Extend and evolve our semantic layer, partnering with domain teams who federate metric definitions on top of it.

The Data Team is building the next-generation data platform - a multi-tenant platform that will become the shared data layer behind our applications. At the heart of that platform is a Python data API built on a layered router → service → repository architecture, containerized with Docker and deployed entirely through infrastructure-as-code. Today the platform is SQL Server-heavy, and part of this role is migrating business and data logic out of legacy stored procedures into testable Python - parameterized SQL for retrieval, pandas for computation and reshaping. title: Human Neuroscientist
description:
About Arbor Neuroscience 
(formerly Forest Neurotech)
Arbor is a nonprofit research organization working on one of the hardest open problems in clinical neuroscience: how to change brain circuits by design.
Millions of people with depression, chronic pain, and other brain disorders have no treatment that works. Modulating activity in the brain circuits underlying their symptoms - with electrical stimulation, focused ultrasound, or magnetic stimulation - can work spectacularly well. But it doesn't work reliably, and we can't predict who it will help.
That's what Arbor aims to fix. The starting point is a new class of experiment: intervene, measure how the circuit responds, track the symptom, and repeat in the same individual over months. We’re building the necessary experimental platform. It currently includes the Forest 1 ultrasound system, which works like a wearable functional MRI, but with higher resolution. The system images activity across large brain volumes, including deep brain structures, and will soon stimulate as well. We are also adding electrode-based interfaces in animal studies. From these data, we'll build models to make neuromodulation predictable.
Arbor is a Focused Research Organization within the Convergent Research family, and the new name for Forest Neurotech. We're a mission-focused nonprofit, doing multidisciplinary translational work that doesn't fit in a lab or on a company roadmap. We have the funding to run the first phase, and we're a small team - the people we hire now will shape what Arbor becomes.

Our benefits include:
Medical, dental, and vision - most plans fully covered for you and your dependents
401(k) with up to 6% match
Company-paid life and AD&D, with voluntary supplemental options
15 holidays plus a floating day for your birthday
3 weeks PTO increasing with tenure, and separate sick leave
Arbor will consider sponsorship for U.S. work authorization case by case. Sponsorship isn't guaranteed, and immigration timelines can affect start dates. Where we sponsor, we cover the legal and government fees.
Arbor is an equal opportunity employer. We hire based on talent and experience and don't discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, disability, age, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

First Entertainment Credit Union is seeking a Member Experience Specialist responsible for delivering outstanding member experience and serving as a knowledgeable, collaborative partner to teammates within the Member Experience Center (MXC). Serving as a Subject Matter Expert (SME), the ideal candidate will deepen new member and existing member relationships by cross-selling products and services.

This role is responsible for owning Helpdesk ticket triage, managing escalated calls, providing coaching to frontline teammates or observation to leaders, and resolving complex requests, and issues in a timely and professional manner. The Member Experience Specialist also supports team development by participating in training initiatives, assisting team members, ensuring adherence to company policies and procedures.

The is a remote position, reporting to the Digital Member Experience Center Manager. External candidates must reside within Arizona, Texas and Georgia to be considered. For pay determination purposes, the target pay in California is between $29 and $35. Offers extended to candidates residing outside of California may be adjusted to reflect the market compensation rates associated with the candidate's geographic location.

Requirements

• Actively listen to members' concerns and provide effective solutions via phone, chat, video appointment and other member service channels, while promoting digital self-service solutions.

• Handle complex member inquiries, complaints, and escalated interactions, ensuring timely and effective resolution.

• Manage HelpDesk tickets and support requests, ensuring accurate research, follow-up, and resolution.

• Collaborate with internal departments to investigate and resolve complex member issues.

• Monitor service queues and escalation trends to identify opportunities for improved service delivery and operational efficiency.

• Review member interactions for quality assurance purposes and provide coaching and feedback to team members and leadership.

• Support onboarding, training, and ongoing development initiatives by providing guidance on MXC procedures, digital tools, systems, and member-facing platforms, while sharing best practices and process updates.

• Assist with operational functions, including transaction overrides, Bill Pay FraudNet reviews, Zelle alerts, token management, TruStage opt-outs, and other specialized tasks as assigned.

• Ensure all member interactions, transactions, and account servicing activities comply with Credit Union policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.

• Identify process improvement opportunities and partner with leadership to enhance member experience, employee effectiveness, and operational performance.

• Accurately document member interactions, resolutions, and recommendations while maintaining confidentiality and data integrity.

At First Entertainment, your role, and every role, is essential to fulfilling our Mission, “We build lifelong relationships with the people of the entertainment and creative industries based on a deep understanding of how they live and work,” and living our Core Values: Members First, Ownership, Integrity, Innovation, Inclusivity, and One Team. We expect all teammates to uphold these principles in everything they do.

Requirements

• High School degree or equivalent required. Two-year college degree or equivalent preferred, or completion of a specialized course of study at a business or trade school.

• A minimum of three (3) to five (5) years’ experience as Financial Service Representative and/or Member Service Representative at a full-service financial institution required.

• Prior experience working in contact center operations and performance metrics required.

• Thorough knowledge of Credit Union products and services, procedures and guidelines, and field of membership requirements.

• Knowledge of digital banking platforms and technologies, such as Alkami, Glia, Wire Xchange, Fiserv, Ensenta,

title: Proposal & RFP Specialist
description:
Magna Legal Services is a trusted nationwide partner to law firms, corporations, insurance carriers, and government agencies, delivering comprehensive legal support at every stage of a case. From court reporting and record retrieval to jury consulting, investigations, litigation graphics, and language services, we help our clients navigate complex legal challenges with confidence. Our reputation is built on the expertise, dedication, and professionalism of our team, and we’re proud to foster a culture where talented people can do meaningful work and grow their careers.

Magna Legal Services is seeking an experienced proposal professional to independently manage our end-to-end RFP response process, from initial intake and planning through final submission. You will support opportunities across Magna’s full range of service lines and client types, including law firms, corporate legal departments, insurance carriers, and government agencies.

RFP volume naturally fluctuates. During active periods, you may manage several concurrent proposals spanning different service lines and buyer types. Outside of active submissions, you will own the infrastructure that makes future responses faster and stronger, including our content and credential libraries, case studies, templates, competitive insights, and proposal processes.

This is an established, full-time area of ownership rather than an entry-level or rotational assignment. You will report directly to the Director of Sales Operations and work with significant autonomy while coordinating closely with Sales, Operations, Marketing, Finance, Legal, IT, HR, and subject-matter experts across the business.

Primary Responsibilities

Proposal Development and Submission

• Own the full lifecycle of RFPs, RFIs, and RFQs, including intake, requirement analysis, project planning, drafting, review coordination, quality assurance, and final submission.

• Review solicitation materials, identify mandatory requirements, and create compliance matrices and workback schedules.

• Draft and edit tailored, persuasive responses across Magna’s service lines, including court reporting and deposition services, jury consulting and research, trial graphics and presentation services, medical record retrieval and review, and language and interpreting services.

• Adapt each response to the buyer’s priorities, recognizing that law firms, corporate legal departments, insurance carriers, and government agencies have different evaluation criteria, compliance requirements, and procurement processes.

• Interview subject-matter experts and business leaders to translate complex operational and technical information into clear, differentiated proposal content.

• Coordinate input and approvals related to pricing, staffing, legal terms, data security, compliance, technology, and implementation.

• Independently manage standard proposal content, including company overviews, service descriptions, staff biographies and credentials, case studies, implementation approaches, and past-performance examples.

• Manage document formatting, version control, review cycles, and submission logistics.

• Ensure every response complies with stated requirements, including page limits, required forms, attachments, certifications, and portal-submission instructions.

• Maintain accurate records of proposal activity, deadlines, submissions, outcomes, and client feedback.
Content and Credential Management

• Build and maintain a centralized, searchable library of approved proposal content.

• Interview consultants and service-line leaders following significant matters to develop compelling case studies and past-performance examples.

• Maintain current biographies, credentials, certifications, and relevant experience for employees and consultants featured in proposals.

• Review and refresh company overviews, service descriptions, methodologies, and differentiators on a regular schedule.

title: People Programs, Strategy, & Operations Director
description:
About EarnIn

As one of the first pioneers of earned wage access, our passion at EarnIn is building products that deliver real-time financial flexibility for those with the unique needs of living paycheck to paycheck. Our community members access their earnings as they earn them, with options to spend, save, and grow their money without mandatory fees, interest rates, or credit checks.

We’re fortunate to have an incredibly experienced leadership team, combined with world-class funding partners like A16Z, Matrix Partners, DST, Ribbit Capital, and a very healthy core business with a tremendous runway. We’re growing fast and are excited to continue bringing world-class talent onboard to help shape the next chapter of our growth journey.

POSITION SUMMARY

This role sits at the center of the People function, driving how we operate, evolve, and deliver at scale. You'll serve as the connective tissue across People sub-teams, bringing rigor, clarity, and momentum to the systems, programs, and initiatives that make the function run. As a builder and strategic operator, you'll shape the infrastructure and culture of how the People team works, while leading high-visibility, high-impact transformation projects on behalf of People leadership.

This is a remote role, with occasional travel to our Mountain View HQ required. The New York Metro base salary range for this full-time position is $201,000-$246,000, plus equity and benefits. Our salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

• Function-wide operations: Own the operating model for the People team - including cross-functional cadences, reporting, dashboards, and the systems that support how we work.

• Core People programs management: Lead end-to-end planning and execution of compensation cycles, performance reviews, and engagement survey activation.
• Note: Not all People moments; sub-teams still need to be accountable for their own execution.

• Transformation & special projects: Drive selective, high-priority, cross-cutting initiatives on behalf of People leadership, including org design, process redesign, and strategic buildouts.

• Sub-team operations: Serve as a central steward of project management, intake, and operational support across People sub-teams.

• AI & automation: Identify and implement opportunities to modernize People workflows through AI tools, automation, and systems improvements.

• Cross-functional liaison: Serve as the primary operational connector between the People team and cohorts like ELT, Finance, Legal, and IT - particularly on transformation initiatives.

• Documentation & knowledge management: Own how the People team captures, stores, and shares its playbooks, SOPs, and program documentation - building a knowledge infrastructure that scales.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

• A systems thinker who also executes - you can zoom out to see the full picture and zoom in to move work forward.

• Experienced in HR/People functions, with a track record of building infrastructure and programs that scale.

• Comfortable owning ambiguous, cross-functional work with senior stakeholders.

• Energized by transformation

• 7+ years of experience in HR, People Operations, or related fields

• Experience using data and data-driven insights to support the business by offering solutions in line with values and business objectives

• Change management skills

• Passion for creating healthy, inclusive organizations where culture is a competitive advantage for a diverse employee population

At EarnIn , we believe that the best way to build a financial system that works for everyday people is by hiring a team that represents our diverse community. Our team is diverse not only in background and experience but also in perspective. We celebrate our diversity and strive to create a culture of belonging. - You'll join at the launch of a new fulfillment center, which means real influence from day one.

- Strong analytical mindset, data-driven decision-making and problem-solving approach

- Excellent communication, coordination and leadership skills

- Proficiency in English, and conversational-level Czech

- Availability to work regular business hours, Monday through Friday, with occasional Saturdays to support operational needs

Nice to have:

- University degree or MBA in a related field

- Experience with Lean, Six Sigma or continuous improvement methodologies

- Experience with routing/dispatch systems, fleet management tools and high-volume delivery operations

What's in it for you

title: Lead Water Treatment Operator
description:
Woodard & Curran is an employee-owned engineering, science, and operations firm dedicated to clean water, a safe environment, healthy communities, and happy people. We foster an inclusive, collaborative culture that supports professional growth, flexibility, and meaningful work, empowering our employees to make a lasting impact on our clients, communities, and the planet.

Woodard & Curran is growing! As part of this growth, we are looking to add a Lead Water Treatment Operator to our water treatment team at the University of New Hampshire (UNH) in Durham, NH. Ideal candidates for this role will hold a minimum of a Grade 3T New Hampshire water treatment license and have a minimum of 5 years of experience.
 
As a Lead Operator, you will take direction from the Plant Manager and help mentor and oversee a more junior-level Operator or Operator in Training, as well as participate in the daily operations and maintenance of the facility. This plant uses conventional surface water treatment including rapid mix flocculation, clarification/sedimentation, and filtration. The plant consists of three separate treatment trains, each having a capacity of 670 gpm, providing 1.88 MGD firm capacity with one train offline.
 
Your primary focus will be in operation and maintenance of the facility’s equipment, process control monitoring and troubleshooting, as well as grounds maintenance.  You will manage process data, perform routine lab analysis, operate SCADA controls and perform computer data entry and other operation and maintenance tasks as directed.
 
Schedule:
 
Employees work a rotating schedule designed to maximize your time off. One week consists of four consecutive workdays (Monday through Thursday) followed by a three-day weekend. The next week includes a day off midweek, and then weekend coverage (Friday through Sunday). This rotation results in a three-day weekend every other week and a scheduled weekday off when working weekend shifts.
 
This position also includes rotating 'on-call' responsibilities to cover after-hour emergencies or alarms, and comes with an additional $200 stipend.
 
Pay Range: $30 - $35 an hour, Depending on qualifications and experience.
 ​
 
What will you be doing at Woodard & Curran?

Monitor water treatment plant processes and equipment both manually and via SCADA automation, making adjustments as necessary to control their operation.
Monitor remote pump stations with inspections and daily sampling as required.
Perform water quality sampling, testing, and analysis to determine compliance with federal, state, and EPA standards.
Operate, maintain, control, and perform routine repair of plant equipment, including preventive maintenance duties. Establish, maintain and control flow through the water treatment process and into and within the distribution system.
Utilize software programs for maintenance work orders and maintains all necessary records.
Perform general maintenance duties of plant and other assigned duties.
Monitors and controls assigned tasks to ensure cost-effective service to meet budget.
Coordinates to ensure that other facility employees follow established administrative, safety, and operating policies.
Oversees operation of assigned treatment, mechanical and electrical equipment and other similarly related facility components and equipment.
Performs data entry and report generation, including data for preparing the Monthly Operating Report.
Assists in maintaining a complete and accurate on-site log book and records on water quality analysis, in accordance with assigned permits.
 
 
What will you need to succeed?

High School Degree or Equivalent.
Massachusetts Grade 3T preferred, 3T OIT accepted with ability to achieve Full status.
Minimum of 2 years’ relevant experience. Equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
Proficiency with computers, including an ability to work with: SCADA, Microsoft Word, Excel, Maintenance Management Programs, and other site specific syst

These systems must perform at scale and deliver exceptional experiences to developers, consumers, and businesses alike.

The team connects product usage and failure patterns with research, evaluation, data, inference, capacity, and external partnerships so that model and product improvements translate into better experiences for users.

 

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a Technical Program Manager to build the flywheel that helps ChatGPT multimodal products learn from real-world usage and improve quickly. You will lead programs spanning production-signal mining, evaluation and data pipelines, research-to-production parity, multimodal capacity planning, and complex cross-functional dependencies for voice and image-generation launches.

You will work closely with product engineering, research, Human Data, inference and capacity teams, safety partners, and external vendors or product partners. Success requires technical depth, strong systems thinking, comfort with ambiguity, and the ability to turn fragmented or manual work into durable mechanisms that teams adopt.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

 

IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

- Build a system for mining production conversations and product signals to identify representative multimodal workflows, user needs, and failure modes.

- Establish and maintain evaluations for the highest-priority multimodal behaviors and use cases, with clear coverage, quality standards, and ownership.

- Package production signals into decision-ready data and evaluations that research teams can use to improve model behavior.

- Measure whether model, prompt, configuration, and product changes produce meaningful improvements in multimodal evaluations and user outcomes.

- Close gaps between research and production environments, including system prompts, sampling behavior, multimodal configurations, inference differences, and other sources of parity drift.

- Create a repeatable process for reproducing product failures with research partners and validating fixes in the shipped experience.

- Lead multimodal capacity planning by forecasting demand, translating it into GPU and serving needs, and managing headroom and reallocation tradeoffs for voice and image-generation workloads.

- Improve the tooling and operating processes used to plan, launch, and operate multimodal capabilities as demand and model behavior evolve.

- Coordinate targeted multilingual data collection across research, Human Data, and external vendors.

- Drive cross-functional programs that multimodal launches depend on, including multimodal actor recruitment and selection and voice-related product partnerships across vehicles, smart speakers, and headphone ecosystems.

- Create clear operating cadences, decision rights, metrics, risk management, and executive-ready communication across complex, time-sensitive programs.

YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

- Have led technically complex programs across machine learning, multimodal products, model evaluation, data pipelines, inference, capacity, or large-scale product infrastructure.

- Can move fluently between user-facing product behavior and the underlying model, evaluation, configuration, serving, and capacity systems.

- Have built mechanisms that convert production signals into prioritized evaluations, data, engineering work, and measurable product improvements.

- Can reason credibly about GPU demand, serving constraints, latency, reliability, quality, and launch tradeoffs.

title: Global Head of Training
description:
THE ROLE 

As Global Head of Training, you'll own the strategy, standards, and operating model for how Wayve trains, certifies, and develops its on-road operational workforce - Vehicle Safety Operators and the teams that support them - across the UK, US, Germany, and Japan. This is a build role: you're accountable for defining the training architecture, building scalable curricula and certification pathways, and proving with data that training is improving readiness, consistency, and safety.

You'll lead a small, globally distributed team of Regional Training Leads and Training Coordinators, translating a single global standard into training that works in each region's operational reality. You'll own the mechanism that turns operational insights, safety findings, and product changes into rapid training updates, and you're the person accountable for whether operators are truly ready before they're deployed on the road.

Key responsibilities:

- Own global training strategy, standards, and operating model across all geographies.

- Define the training architecture: scalable curricula, onboarding pathways, and certification frameworks for on-road and maintenance operational roles.

- Own operational readiness - ensuring operators meet performance and safety thresholds before live on-road deployment.

- Build and maintain the mechanism for converting product requirements and operational insights into rapid, targeted training updates.

- Establish and own the metrics and reporting that prove training effectiveness, readiness, and adherence - and use that data to prioritise interventions.

- Manage and develop Regional Training Leads, holding them accountable to a consistent global standard while enabling local adaptation.

- Partner cross-functionally with Operations, Product, and Safety to align training outcomes with business and operational needs.

- Own certification and compliance record-keeping standards globally, ensuring accuracy and audit-readiness.

To give the best experience to Doctolibers and support Doctolib’s growth, you will help manage our IT stock and asset base, including laptops, smartphones and accessories. Reporting to the IT team, you will own the reliability of our hardware inventory and contribute to day-to-day on-site support in an international environment across Germany, France, Italy and the Netherlands.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

As a Working Student, you will support us in the following areas:

IT stock and asset management - approximately 70%

- Manage the site’s IT stock, including receiving, checking, labelling and storing laptops, smartphones and accessories

- Keep the inventory up to date in our asset management tool and ensure the accuracy of serial numbers, assignments and statuses

- Follow the full equipment lifecycle, including assignment, return, loan, vendor repair, refurbishment and recycling

- Run periodic physical inventories and consistency checks between physical stock and the asset management tool

- Monitor stock levels, flag replenishment thresholds and contribute to supplier orders

- Prepare devices, including mobile device management enrolment, standard configuration and accessory kits

- Propose improvements to stock processes, documentation, automation and key performance indicators

On-site support - approximately 30%

- Support onboarding and offboarding by preparing, handing over and recovering equipment for joiners and leavers

- Run the Berlin IT Corner as a physical point of contact for Doctolibers

- Manage meeting room hardware by testing, updating and replacing equipment

- Handle level 1 requests and incidents, including basic diagnosis and application access, and escalate to level 2 when needed

- Identify recurring requests and contribute to continuous improvement

WORKING WITH US, YOU WILL LEARN:

- How to manage the full lifecycle of IT hardware and maintain reliable asset data

- How on-site IT support contributes to a smooth employee experience

- How to identify opportunities to improve operational processes through documentation, automation and performance indicators

WHO YOU ARE

If you don't have the exact profile described below, but you feel this job description matches your skill set, we still encourage you to apply.

YOU COULD BE OUR NEXT TEAM MATE IF YOU:

- You are enrolled full-time at a university, ideally studying IT Systems Management, IT Management, Applied IT or a related field

- You are rigorous, organised and service-oriented, with good interpersonal skills

- You are comfortable working with Windows, macOS, iOS and Android, and can prioritise tasks while working autonomously and as part of a team

- You are fluent in German and English

- You are able to work on site in Berlin and handle equipment weighing up to 25 kg

NOW, IT WOULD BE FANTASTIC IF YOU:

- You have had a first exposure to an IT service management or mobile device management tool

WHAT WE OFFER

- A structured and personalized onboarding program through our Doctolib Academy, as well as a wide range of in-house training opportunities

- A flexible working model that allows for hybrid and office-based work

- A Deutschlandticket sponsored by Doctolib, or reimbursement of your semester ticket

- 28 vacation days per year (calculated pro rata according to your working schedule)

- The opportunity to work from abroad for up to 10 days per year (eligible after 6 months)

- Company health insurance with many additional benefits and subsidies (eligible after 6 months)

- Regular breakfast in the office and subsidies for your lunch or grocery shopping

- A subsidized sports program with our partner Urban Sports Club

THE INTERVIEW PROCESS

- Interview with a team mate

- Interview with your future Manager

title: HPC Performance Engineer
description:
NVIDIA has been transforming computer graphics, PC gaming, and accelerated computing for more than 25 years. It’s a unique legacy of innovation that’s fueled by great technology-and amazing people.
Today, we’re tapping into the unlimited potential of AI to define the next era of computing. An era in which our GPU acts as the brains of computers, robots, and self-driving cars that can understand the world. Doing what’s never been done before takes vision, innovation, and the world’s best talent. As an NVIDIA N, you’ll be immersed in a diverse, supportive environment where everyone is inspired to do their best work. Come join the team and see how you can make a lasting impact on the world.
We are looking for a HPC Performance Engineer in our NVHPC compilers & tools group. Our performance engineers analyze High Performance Computing (HPC) applications with the intent of improving performance by driving compiler optimizations and library enhancements. This role offers the chance to work with a wide range of applications, from small benchmarks running on single-CPU core to full-scale applications running on multi-node multi-GPU systems. You'll find optimization opportunities and work closely with our compiler development and application engineering teams to deliver effective solutions.
What you'll be doing:

• Analyze the effect of different compilers and compiler optimizations on HPC application performance.

• Evaluate whether and how the compiler and runtime can improve the performance of key HPC applications on CPU and CPU/GPU platforms.

• Communicate limits of compiler capabilities with application engineering to guide the best path forward towards improving performance.

• Port HPC applications to different platforms and programming models.

• Evaluate the impact of NVHPC package components, device driver, and system configuration on application performance.

What we need to see:

• BS/MS or equivalent experience in Computer Science or a related engineering field.

• 5+ years of programming experience.

• Solid understanding of Fortran, C, C++, and programming techniques, especially for parallel architectures, preferably for compilers.

• Experience with OpenACC, OpenMP, MPI, CUDA and Standard Language Parallelism.

• Strong skills in performance analysis and tuning, as well as a broad understanding of parallel applications development tools and runtime environments.

• Strong mathematical fundamentals, including linear algebra and numerical methods.

• Understand performance considerations, tradeoffs, and impact.

• Expert interpersonal skills, a logical approach to problem-solving, good time management, and task prioritization skills. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, along with the ability to work in a dynamic development team.

Ways to stand out from the crowd:

• You have a deep understanding of machine architectures and micro-architectures.

• Experience with debugging and porting as well as assembly language programming is a significant advantage.

NVIDIA is committed to fostering a diverse work environment and proud to be an equal opportunity employer. As we highly value diversity in our current and future employees, we do not discriminate (including in our hiring and promotion practices) on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status or any other characteristic protected by law.
Widely considered to be one of the technology world’s most desirable employers, NVIDIA offers highly competitive salaries and a comprehensive benefits package. As you plan your future, see what we can offer to you and your family www.nvidiabenefits.com/
